The second most common malignancy and the leading cause of death among women in developing countries. Seventy-five percent of the patients present in advanced stages; lack of organized screening programmes for detection of
the preclinical stages in many countries contributes to the late presentation.
Two age groups with highest incidence: 35 - 40 years; 45 - 55 years
Aetiology
Human papilloma virus (HPV) infection. The infection is usually acquired through sexual intercourse.
